passage.title: Model answer written for TGA
paras: Both writers present the flood as a disaster that reveals unexpected kindness, although the memoir focuses on one street while the letter speaks for a whole valley. [Point] The memoir's Mr Hale, who 'complained about our football for years', hands over a loaf, whereas the letter praises mill-hands who 'formed a chain across the bridge'. [Evidence] The modern writer uses a single, gently comic example, while the nineteenth-century writer uses formal, public praise. [Methods] Both suggest that crisis can turn neighbours and workers into a community. [Concept] Ultimately, the memoir's final line, that some neighbours 'never went back to being strangers', makes the change feel lasting, while the letter ends with an appeal for help. [Synthesis]

questions.q: Annotate the Q3 model points: which language and which structural features does it use?
questions.a: Language: 'Shoes on' calm speech, personified water, senses; structure: tension builds to the turn 'What I remember most', reflective final line.
questions.model: Teacher annotates the first two sentences: language point ('very calmly' more frightening than shouting) and its effect; then the structural turn to kindness.
